notes.decision: The Coptic numeral ⲣ̄ⲓ = 110. Marks chapter 110 of the Kephalaia. Repeated possibly as marginal numeral at incipit and continuing-mark at line-end. Final ⲣ̄ⲓ may also be the start of a wrapped word truncated by lacuna.
ⲧⲃⲁ = myriad (10,000), ⲭⲟⲩⲧⲏ = twenty. So 'a myriad of twenty' = twenty myriads = 200,000. Standard Coptic numerical compound for large numbers.
Per glossary ⲧⲁⲃⲉϩ = 'seal' (Lyc reflex of ⲧⲱⲃⲉ). The 200,000 seals in the body of man relate to the Manichaean micro-cosmology of body as cosmic structure with sealed light-particles.

Conjunctive 3pl forms: 'they are chosen' (ⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄ 'choose' Lyc ⲥⲱⲧϩ) + 'they are purified' (ⲧⲟⲩⲃⲟ). The triple sequence ⲛⲉⲥⲱⲧϩ / ⲛⲥⲉⲧⲟⲩⲃⲟ / ⲛ̄ⲥⲉⲉⲓ ⲁϩⲟⲩⲛ = 'be chosen, be purified, come inward' describes the Manichaean refinement of light-particles within the body of man — the chapter's correspondential schema.

Physically preserved word of uncertain meaning. In context of triple parallelism ⲍⲙ ⲡⲍⲣⲁⲩ ⲍⲙ ⲡⲥⲉ ⲍⲙ ⲡⲣ̄..., I have tentatively rendered as 'speech' (suspecting Lyc reduction of ⲡⲥⲉⲭⲉ 'word/saying'). Alternative readings: 'time' (ⲥⲏⲩ→ⲥⲉ), 'occasion' (ⲥⲉⲡ), or possibly an unidentified sense-domain term. Confidence low.

Translated 'myriads of archons' tentatively. ⲟ̄ⲁⲥ is unattested in our corpus; possibly Lycopolitan reflex of ⲟⲩⲁⲥⲉ 'multitude' or numerical/quantifier word. Could alternatively be 'voice' (ⲟⲩⲁⲥ) but doesn't fit syntax with ⲛ̄ⲁⲣⲭⲱⲛ.
